title: docs(skills): teach that a save and os validate refuse titleFormat

_Requested by **Irene** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01TJXtQ1tVD26ecLDZxFS67x?thread=cmsg_01TJXtQ1tVD26ecLDZxFS67x7p5hEJsCWtDpFXteTCt847)_

Fixes #29506

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

The maintainer waived the model-tier mandate for `skills/**` while that tier had no quota; this PR was developed below it.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:两个技能不再把 `titleFormat` 讲成「已弃用但未移除」,改为「保存和 `os validate` 会拒绝它(`title-format-retired`),改用 `nameField`」;ADR-0079 D3 加一条带日期的修订说明,引用裁决 6574393684 和 PR #29499。决定本身不动。
- 为什么改:PR #29499 已让保存门和 `os validate` 拒绝写了 `titleFormat` 的对象,三处文本还在教旧规则(「advisory, not an error」)。
- 风险与回滚:纯文本 + changeset,无代码改动。两个技能文件都变小(data 6119 → 6116 tokens,formula 5956 → 5950),无 re-wrap,上限未动。回滚即 revert。
- 先看:`skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` 的 `titleFormat` 行;`docs/adr/0079-record-display-name.md` D3 下的 Amendment 块。
- 需要你做的:Tier H 受管面(`skills/**`),契约复审后需要 `GOVERNED_APPROVERS` 批准;PR 保持 draft。

## What changes

The refusal is read off main, not the card: `packages/lint/src/validate-record-title.ts` (`validateTitleFormatRetired`, severity `error`, rule `title-format-retired`, registered in `authoring-rules.ts` with `surfaces: CLI_AND_RUNTIME`) and `packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-title-format-refused.ts` ("`os validate`, `os build`, `os lint` and the metadata save gate (`422 INVALID_METADATA`) refuse the key as `title-format-retired`, an error").

- `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`, the `titleFormat` row of the optional-properties table:
  - Before: `**Deprecated, not removed (ADR-0079)** — render-only: the server can't return or query it. Use `nameField` (it wins); a composite title follows the `nameField` row`
  - After: `**Refused (ADR-0079)**: a save and `os validate` refuse it (`title-format-retired`). Move it to `nameField`; a composite title follows the `nameField` row`
  - The render-only reason is dropped: its home is `os explain title-format-retired` (the lint fix line points there, `validate-record-title.ts` [#22161] comment) and ADR-0079 D3. "(it wins)" is dropped because precedence no longer matters once the key is refused.
- `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md`, the `template` row's carriers cell: `Object.titleFormat` (deprecated → `nameField`, ADR-0079) becomes `Object.titleFormat` (a save and `os validate` refuse it; move it to `nameField`, ADR-0079). Paid by deleting the sentence below the table "a template holds a path and a formatter, nothing else.", which restates the same row's Grammar cell (`{{ path }}` or `{{ path | formatter[:arg] }}`, no conditionals). "Move logic into a CEL field" stays; the two lines around the cut are otherwise byte-identical, no re-wrap.
- `docs/adr/0079-record-display-name.md`: a dated amendment block directly under the D3 heading, citing ruling 6574393684 (#29007, letter B) and PR #29499 (`3557366c02`). It says the key is *refused, not removed* (the schema still parses it, so a stored object keeps loading until its next save), which keeps the wording consistent with Open question 3's remark that "retired" is used for a key that is still live. It names the "deprecated and lint-warned" and "advisory, not an error" sentences as describing the code before #29499, and notes D8's "never errors" no longer covers `title-format-retired`. D8 carries a one-line `Amended (2026-11-04, #29506)` pointer back to the D3 note (D8's own text is unchanged), and the status line gains `· **Amended** (2026-11-04, #29506, ruling 6574393684 …)` in the ADR-0045 form. D3's decision and its quoted citation are left as they are.
- `.changeset/29506-title-format-refused-teaching.md`: `'@objectstack/skills': patch`, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`.

### Token ratchet (no ceiling row moved, no re-wrap)

| `skills/objectstack-formula/SKILL.md` | 5956 / 5950 / 5997 | 23842 / 23819 |

## Why

PR #29499 made a save and `os validate` refuse an authored `titleFormat` (ruling 6574393684). The skills still taught "deprecated, not removed" and the ADR still said "advisory, not an error", so an author following them would write a key the platform refuses.
